clue.text: Couple concluding Kerouac stops grand lady — is this On The Road?

definitions.note: a road surface is what lies on the road; the clue's question invites the answer as a thing

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside another like a stopper

parts.note: a madam is a formal title for a grand lady

indicators.note: a couple is two, and what concludes a word is its tail, so the closing pair of letters is kept

parts.note: the final couple of letters of the writer's surname

explanation.surface: A wry nod to Jack Kerouac's novel On The Road, with a grand lady in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerouac's famous novel title is the definition in disguise: read literally, it describes what is laid on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is the crushed-stone surfacing laid on highways, named after the engineer John McAdam.

clue.text: Upset about party's position that's sometimes silly?

indicators.note: to be about something is to go around it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to miff someone is to upset or annoy them
a do is an informal party; the apostrophe-s is just 'is' joining to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about where a political party stands, a stance that can look silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party’s position' reads as politics, but this is cricket. Mid-off is a fielding position; brought very close to the bat it is called 'silly mid-off'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a fielder placed near the batter in that spot is named silly mid-off, so the position is sometimes silly.

clue.text: Anglican carrying iron rod in drinking establishment

indicators.note: whatever carries something holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: C of E, the Church of England, stands for Anglican
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a bar is a rod of metal

explanation.surface: A churchman carries an iron rod into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking establishment' suggests alcohol, but coffee is drunk too. C OF E is the usual abbreviation for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee bar is a small cafe where people go for hot drinks, so it is a place set up for drinking.

clue.text: Bits of information concealed in play's model scene

indicators.note: what is concealed in something is tucked away inside it

parts.note: a drama is a play; the apostrophe-s is 'is' joining wordplay to definition
binary bits are ones and zeros, written as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Snippets of information are hidden in a play's model set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits' are binary digits, 1 and 0, which crosswords render as the look-alike letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional miniature representation of a scene, often in a museum display case.

clue.text: What milliners do, bringing up small ecstasy rush

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing up the small letter lifts it one place higher, swapping it with its neighbour

parts.note: milliners make hats; its final small letter is the one lifted
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Hat-makers at work get a rush from a little ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take MAKE HATS, raise the small S one place above the T, then add E. 'Small' points to S, the usual abbreviation, which is the letter moved.
explanation.definitionFit: To make haste is an old-fashioned idiom for hurrying, which is what rushing means.

clue.text: Note muddle about one Aristotelian literary term

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a mess is a muddle
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A confused note about one of Aristotle's critical terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a jotting, but crosswords often mean a sol-fa note: do, re, mi and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimesis, imitation or representation of reality in art, is a key concept in Aristotle's Poetics.

clue.text: Tinker picked up award for achievement

indicators.note: to pick something up can mean to catch it by ear, so we go by sound

parts.note: to tinker with something is to meddle with it

explanation.surface: A tinker collected a prize for his accomplishments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as collected, but here it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is a metal disc presented in recognition of distinction, bravery or success.

clue.text: Stick up hotel, beset by drunk police still

parts.note: to mug is to rob, as in a stick-up

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A robbery of a hotel in which drunk police stand still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb, but it is a noun: a still photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is a photograph of a suspect's face taken by police on arrest, a static image for records.

clue.text: Alluring person about to feed lust?

indicators.note: food that feeds something goes into it, so one piece is placed inside

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A seductive person about to stoke someone's desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is RE and 'to feed' is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren, from the mythical singers who lured sailors, is a dangerously attractive woman.

clue.text: Maybe Leo Delibes's finale getting poor ratings

indicators.note: poor work is badly put together, so these letters are rearranged
a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter is wanted

parts.note: the composer's surname ends in this letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps the composer Leo Delibes's final work got bad reviews.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo Delibes was a real French composer, so 'Leo' feels like his first name; it is the zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve zodiac constellations used in astrology, so it is an example.

clue.text: Sacked US lawman's flipping stunned

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent; the apostrophe-s is 'is'
to be rocked is to be shocked or stunned

explanation.surface: A fired American law officer is reeling in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' could be a mild British oath, but it reverses FED.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrocked describes a priest formally dismissed from the clergy, a specific way of being dismissed from office.

clue.text: In Ireland, force a tedious person back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a drag is a bore

explanation.surface: In Ireland, someone forces a bore to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a police service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is the national police service of the Republic of Ireland, usually called simply the Garda.

clue.text: AI's eschewed in fair vote returning revered figure

parts.note: the word with its A and I removed

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
what is eschewed is avoided, so those letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to remove; the apostrophe-s is 'is'
aye is a vote in favour

explanation.surface: Artificial intelligence is banned from a fair election to honour a revered figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AI’s' is not artificial intelligence here but simply two letters to strike out.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and fertility, a deity worshipped and honoured in Scandinavian myth.

clue.text: Veterans on horse behave touchingly?

indicators.note: in an across entry one thing on another comes after it, so the first-named part goes second

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
old hands are experienced veterans

explanation.surface: Old soldiers on horseback behaving tenderly.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' puts the first part after the second. 'Horse' is slang for heroin, written H.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding hands is literally a touching gesture, and the question mark flags the pun on emotionally moving.

clue.text: Two sons getting a good deal on underwear item? It's worth little

definitions.note: a sentence about the thing; the answer is the thing itself

indicators.note: in an across entry one thing on another follows it, so the first-named part goes second

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
S for son, twice
far means a good deal, as in far better
a thing is an item

explanation.surface: Two sons snap up a bargain on lingerie that turns out nearly worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwear item' looks like one unit but splits around the sons and the deal. A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not worth a brass farthing is an idiom for near-worthlessness, the coin being the tiniest money.

clue.text: Machiavellian characteristic of speech breaking friendship

indicators.note: to break into something is to force a way inside it

parts.note: amity is friendship
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A scheming manner of talking that ruins a friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characteristic of speech' reads as a quality of speaking, but 'of speech' alone is the spoken-word adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Machiavelli advised rulers to ignore ethics for power, so lacking moral scruple is the trait his name evokes.

clue.text: I'm stunned by that tambourine Verdi deftly incorporates

indicators.note: to incorporate something is to contain it as part of the body, so the letters lie within the run of words

parts.note: the letters run across the word boundaries of this phrase

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished at how skilfully Verdi wrote in a tambourine part.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'tambourine' through 'Verdi' into 'deftly'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Well, I never did!' is a dated exclamation of surprise, used to express amazement.

clue.text: Liberal, in a loud voice, gets excited

indicators.note: this word places one piece within the other

parts.note: taken as written
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
to voice is to utter

explanation.surface: A Liberal speaking loudly gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' is a verb here, giving UTTER; L slips between A F and UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter means nervously agitated or thrilled, like a heart that flutters in anticipation.

clue.text: One tells a future doctor to get in to free uni, oddly

indicators.note: to get in is to enter, so one piece goes inside another
doing something oddly means in a strange arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
to cook the books is to doctor them

explanation.surface: Someone advises an aspiring medic to get into a free university, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' usually means take odd letters; here it rearranges the whole phrase. 'Future doctor' looks like a medical student, but 'doctor' is a verb meaning falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune cookie is a crisp biscuit holding a paper slip that predicts what lies ahead.

clue.text: This will soothe female leaving work

indicators.note: what is leaving departs, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to work is to function
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Something calming for a woman quitting her job.
explanation.walkthrough: FUNCTION loses its initial F.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is anointing with oil or ointment, and also a soothing salve applied to the skin.

clue.text: With luck, Ken's rolling a joint

indicators.note: rolling things tumble over and over, ending in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: With a bit of luck, Ken is rolling a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A joint' suggests a cannabis cigarette; it is a body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A knuckle is a finger joint, where the bones of the hand meet and bend.

clue.text: Join in mission to follow TikTok or Instagram?

parts.note: both are smartphone apps
an end is an aim or mission

explanation.surface: Signing up to a cause on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the two platforms are only examples of the category wanted, not the answer themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach or add something on, so it means to join one thing to another.

clue.text: You heard right: cover of iconic song creates irritation

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by ear, so we go by sound

parts.note: the single letter is pronounced the same as the pronoun
RT is an abbreviation for right

indicators.note: a cover wraps the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a cover version of a classic song is grating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version, but it means the outside letters of 'iconic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is the medical name for hives, an itchy rash that inflames the skin.

clue.text: Gathered scripture up showing distinctive symbol

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: people who gathered met
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Collected religious texts held up as a distinctive emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: MET and OT together, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem venerated as the sign of a clan, and more loosely any emblematic symbol.

clue.text: Explore area for play, given limits of Cymbeline

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field

indicators.note: limits are boundaries at each end, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the play's title

explanation.surface: Scouting out the setting for a stage production of Shakespeare's Cymbeline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' and 'Cymbeline' suggest theatre, but the play is a playground. Recce is British slang for a reconnaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: To recce is informal British for to reconnoitre, surveying an area before acting there.

clue.text: Don't leave any energy drink bottles behind for all to see

definitions.note: an instruction rather than a plain verb, but it means the same

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold in a container, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Litter advice: don't abandon energy-drink bottles for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' looks like one product but splits. 'Behind' puts SUP holding E after U.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up something is to consume all of it, leaving nothing remaining.

clue.text: Taunt Stoic regularly? Everyone must join in

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and following letters

explanation.walkthrough: Take every other letter of 'Taunt Stoic', starting with the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is an Italian musical direction telling the full orchestra or choir to play or sing together.

clue.text: US singer's swish and mostly eager to receive publicity

parts.note: swish means smart or stylish, as does chic

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: keen minus its last letter
an ad is publicity

explanation.walkthrough: 'US singer' suggests a celebrity, but it is a songbird. KEEN loses its N, then takes AD inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickadee is a small North American bird of the tit family, known for its call.

clue.text: Exciting tale shot on camera briefly

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so its last letter goes
something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
the word minus its final letter

explanation.surface: A thrilling story filmed quickly on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like filming, which fits the surface, but it signals a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a story of adventure or love, originally a medieval tale of chivalry.

clue.text: Yankee flourished, putting away whiskey provided

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to put something away is to remove it from view, so that letter goes

parts.note: to flourish a sword is to wield it
W is Whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
